extracted.action: FDA established a 'green list' import alert, Import Alert 66-80, to help stop GLP-1 active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) that have potential quality concerns from entering the U.S. supply chain.
extracted.how_it_works: The green list will include GLP-1 APIs from facilities the agency has inspected or evaluated that appear to be in compliance with FDA's standards. APIs from unverified foreign sources are the target.
extracted.revision_date_anchor: A major revision of Import Alert 66-80 was made in response to a CDER Office of Compliance, Office of Manufacturing Quality, Division of Drug Quality memo dated March 19, 2026. Exact press announcement date NOT confirmed.
extracted.stated_background: FDA previously identified serious concerns with compounded versions of semaglutide and tirzepatide, including dosing errors, use of unapproved salt forms and adverse events, some requiring hospitalization.
extracted.SUPPLY_CHAIN_IMPLICATION: FDA treats the API supply feeding compounded GLP-1s as a quality risk requiring an import gate. This means the identity and quality of the active ingredient in any given compounded GLP-1 product is not something a consumer-facing tool can characterize, let alone price-compare. There is no product identity to hold constant across sellers.
extracted.THIRD_INDEPENDENT_LOCK: This is a third independent regulatory barrier alongside shortage-list removal and the 503B bulks exclusion proposal - a restriction on the raw material itself.
